artboards.title: 3 · Proposed Home on today's real data

annotations.text:
Sprouttie Home proposal

Read left to right. These are static mockups, not a clickable prototype: the job is to make an argument, not to test an interaction.

Unchecked assumptions — the bath-time prompts and the dinosaur-book line assume the "12 saved" books and "3 tips" on today's dashboard are real content stores rather than placeholders. Neither was traced, which is why they appear flagged on board 3 rather than drawn as working.

1 · Home today

Recreated from Dashboard.jsx, not traced from a screenshot.

Metrics first, and the one number that matters is buried in a status line: "Last session: 30 days ago". Nothing here tells you what to do now.

2 · Proposed Home, once promotion works

One directive block, one primary action, then the reward strip. This is the version worth building — but only after board 4 is settled.

Nav drops to four tabs with Log absorbed into Home. "Words Said" keeps its full name rather than shortening to "Words".

3 · The same design on today's real data

Rendered against 110 / 0 / 0. The reward strip is empty, and two of the three routine steps have no content behind them.

This is what would actually ship if the screen were built before the rule. It is the board that matters.

4 · The decision that unblocks it

Three candidate promotion rules, each with its data cost and its honest tradeoff. Option C is outlined in green as the leading candidate: it needs no new capture, and the daily_tracking join it depends on is the one just fixed. That is a recommendation, not a decision.

"Would promote today" reads [run query] for options A and C — those numbers would be invented otherwise. Both are fillable with one query against spoken_words and daily_tracking.
